[bugfix] Mark draft tokens to rebuilt their embeddings. (#57356)

Signed-off-by: HieDean <799287043@qq.com>
Co-authored-by: hiedean <hiedean@tju.edu.cn>

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: Upstream commit 493d4b3c04a4 fixes GPUModelRunner._prepare_input_ids (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py): in the enable_prompt_embeds path under async scheduling, draft tokens are scattered directly into input_ids.gpu, so the code now marks those positions in the CPU-side is_token_ids mask (`if spec_flattened_indices: self.is_token_ids.np[spec_flattened_indices] = True`) before `self.is_token_ids.copy_to_gpu(total_num_scheduled_tokens)` so their embeddings are rebuilt. The mainline 910B paths need no change: NPUModelRunner V1 (vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py) and V2 (vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py) inherit upstream GPUModelRunner._prepare_input_ids without overriding it (only called via self._prepare_input_ids), so they pick up the fix on the vllm version bump. The only vllm-ascend code that requires adaptation is the forked copy of _prepare_input_ids in NPUModelRunner310 (vllm_ascend/_310p/model_runner_310p.py:867), maintained because of a tensor.copy_ accuracy workaround. Its enable_prompt_embeds branches (lines ~916-920 and the common-case optimization at ~928-929) refresh is_token_ids.gpu from the CPU copy without marking the spec_flattened_indices positions as True, so draft-token embeddings can be stale on 310P with prompt-embeds + async scheduling + spec decode. Adaptation: mirror the upstream fix in this fork, e.g. before refreshing the GPU mask add `if spec_flattened_indices: self.is_token_ids.np[spec_flattened_indices] = True` alongside `self.is_token_ids.copy_to_gpu(total_num_scheduled_tokens)`, keeping the existing copy_/index_copy_ workaround intact. The `is_token_ids.np[...] = True` write is a pure-CPU numpy op on the buffer created by the parent runner, so it is NPU-safe.
deep_analysis.risk: Low. The change is a 3-line correctness fix confined to the prompt-embeds (multimodal/prompt embedding) + async-scheduling + speculative-decode path. Only the 310P runner fork needs manual sync; the 910B V1/V2 runners inherit it automatically. Risk is limited to forgetting to keep the 310P fork in sync (stale draft-token embeddings on 310P) or introducing a regression in the forked copy_/index_copy_ logic if the fix is applied carelessly. No new CPU<->NPU sync is introduced (numpy write to CPU mask plus existing copy_to_gpu).

affected_interfaces: vllm_ascend/worker/v2/input_batch.py — AscendInputBatch.make_dummy classmethod (signature lacks is_padding; must accept and forward it)
vllm_ascend/worker/v2/aclgraph_utils.py — _prepare_pcp_inputs_to_capture (line 70) calls AscendInputBatch.make_dummy; needs to stay compatible with new signature

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: This commit (861a299adc72) adds is_padding=not is_profile to InputBatch.make_dummy in GPUModelRunner.execute_model's dummy branch. vllm-ascend is a true positive because patch/worker/patch_v2/patch_input_batch.py rebinds model_runner.InputBatch = AscendInputBatch, so the upstream call now hits AscendInputBatch.make_dummy, which does not accept is_padding -> TypeError on every dummy run (profile_run, warmup/ACL-graph capture, DP idle ranks). Required changes: 1) In vllm_ascend/worker/v2/input_batch.py, extend AscendInputBatch.make_dummy with 'is_padding: bool = True' and forward it to InputBatch.make_dummy(num_reqs, num_tokens, input_buffers, max_query_len=max_query_len, is_padding=is_padding) so the is_padding buffer is filled correctly and flows into the returned batch's base_fields. 2) Verify vllm_ascend/worker/v2/aclgraph_utils.py:_prepare_pcp_inputs_to_capture and the 310P make_dummy wrappers (_310p/worker/v2/aclgraph.py, _310p/worker/v2/spec_decode/aclgraph.py) still work; they currently pass no is_padding (default True, matching prior behavior). 3) Behavioral alignment: with is_padding=False during profile_run, dummy tokens now route through AscendMoERunner so MoE memory/kernels are exercised during profiling (the commit's intent). Ascend routers (AscendFusedTopKRouter/AscendGroupedTopKRouter) do not read forward_context.is_padding to skip routing, so routing occurs either way; but DeepSeek V4 / Kimi K3 SP paths do read forward_context.is_padding via sp_padding_mask under VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING (vllm_ascend/models/deepseek_v4/model.py:936-938, mtp.py, dspark.py, kimi_k3.py:694-697), so confirm profiling/SP-mask behavior on those models. 4) Validate memory profiling for MoE models (with override_mrv2_in_profile_run and MC2 token-capacity dummy runs in profile_run) since profiled peak memory may increase. 5) Run tests/ut/worker tests (test_model_runner_v2.py, test_pcp_manager_v2.py) plus an NPU startup/profile_run sanity check.
deep_analysis.risk: High if unaddressed: every vllm-ascend startup fails with TypeError: make_dummy() got an unexpected keyword argument 'is_padding' during profile_run/warmup (NPUModelRunnerV2 inherits upstream execute_model dummy branch via NPUModelRunnerV2._dummy_run/execute_model). After the mechanical signature fix, medium risk remains: profiling now routes dummy tokens to MoE experts, changing measured MoE memory for DeepSeek V4 / Kimi K3 / gpt-oss etc.; must verify it does not over-reserve or break MC2/EPLB buffer pre-allocation and that SP is_padding masks (sp_padding_mask) behave correctly with an all-False dummy mask during profiling. DP idle-rank dummy runs keep is_padding=True, preserving current behavior.

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
The commit is primarily XPU enablement but includes a cross-platform rename in the shared EPLB runtime that breaks Ascend's async EPLB integration. Required changes:

1. vllm_ascend/distributed/eplb/state.py (AscendEplbState):
   - Rename the `cuda_device_index` annotation and all `self.cuda_device_index` references to `device_index` (lines ~96, 101-102).
   - Critical: upstream EplbState.__init__ now only populates `device_index` when `device.type in ("cuda", "xpu")`; on Ascend device.type is "npu", so it stays None. AscendEplbState must explicitly set `self.device_index = torch.accelerator.current_device_index()` when None (mirroring the old behavior it implemented via cuda_device_index).
   - Without this, EplbState.add_model() passes device_index=None to EplbModelState and start_async_worker() in vllm/distributed/eplb/async_worker.py asserts `device_index is not None` → AssertionError at startup. Since Ascend forces eplb_config.use_async=True (vllm_ascend/platform.py:925-931), this path is always exercised when --enable-eplb is set on NPU.

2. tests/ut/distributed/eplb/test_state.py:
   - Rename test_init_sets_cuda_device_index_for_npu to assert `state.device_index == 5` (and rename test accordingly).

3. vllm_ascend/distributed/eplb/communicator.py (AscendGlooEplbCommunicator):
   - The base TorchDistGlooStagedEplbCommunicator constructor param/attr was renamed cuda_stream→stream and its execute() now uses the new portable device_stream()/torch.accelerator instead of torch.cuda. The Ascend subclass does not reference _cuda_stream/_stream directly, so no code change is required, but add/update a UT to confirm the subclass still works with the new base execute() (it now avoids torch.cuda calls, which is beneficial on NPU).

4. No action needed for: TorchDistXCCLStagedEplbCommunicator (XPU-only), device_stream()/torch.Event in eplb_utils.py (portable, replaces torch.cuda.Event which Ascend previously had to monkeypatch), ParallelConfig is_xpu() EPLB gate (Ascend still passes via the _CudaAlikeEplbPlatformProxy in patch_eplb.py), base_router.py EPLB Triton kernel enablement (XPU-only; Ascend uses its own routers in vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/router/), and xpu_moe.py (XPU-only).
deep_analysis.risk: If unaddressed, enabling EPLB on Ascend (Model Runner V2, which Ascend requires) will crash with `AssertionError` in start_async_worker because the renamed device_index is never populated on npu devices, breaking MoE expert-parallel load-balancing startup. Low-to-moderate overall risk since the fix is a focused rename plus explicit device_index initialization and one test update; the remaining EPLB changes in this commit are additive (XPU communicator) or platform-neutral (torch.accelerator/device_stream), so no other Ascend paths are at risk.

[Scheduler] Add --max-num-active-seqs to cap RUNNING admission (#56758)

Signed-off-by: Li <chuali@amd.com>
Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

affected_interfaces: DyntraLBScheduler.schedule() / DyntraLBAsyncScheduler (vllm_ascend/core/dyntra_lb_scheduler.py) — vendored schedule() admission loop still caps RUNNING on max_num_running_reqs
RecomputeScheduler.schedule() / AsyncRecomputeScheduler (vllm_ascend/core/recompute_scheduler.py) — vendored schedule() admission loop uses max_num_running_reqs
ProfilingChunkScheduler.schedule() (vllm_ascend/core/scheduler_profiling_chunk.py) — vendored schedule() admission loop uses max_num_running_reqs
RecomputeSchedulerConfig.initialize_from_config (vllm_ascend/core/recompute_scheduler.py) — dynamic field copy already carries max_num_active_seqs automatically; no manual change needed
deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: Upstream commit f730a93d2bf2 adds SchedulerConfig.max_num_active_seqs (default None, ge=1, validated <= max_num_seqs), the --max-num-active-seqs CLI arg, and computes Scheduler.max_num_active_reqs (falls back to max_num_running_reqs) which now gates WAITING->RUNNING admission instead of max_num_running_reqs. Because vllm-ascend vendors full copies of the upstream schedule() method in three custom schedulers, the new cap will be silently ignored on Ascend (no error, no effect) until those vendored admission checks are updated. Required changes: (1) vllm_ascend/core/dyntra_lb_scheduler.py ~line 676: change `if num_running >= self.max_num_running_reqs:` to `if num_running >= self.max_num_active_reqs:` in the WAITING scheduling loop; (2) vllm_ascend/core/recompute_scheduler.py ~line 444: same change in RecomputeScheduler.schedule(); (3) vllm_ascend/core/scheduler_profiling_chunk.py ~line 479: change `if len(self.running) == self.max_num_running_reqs:` to use `self.max_num_active_reqs`. `max_num_active_reqs` is already computed in the inherited base Scheduler.__init__ since these classes subclass vllm.v1.core.sched.scheduler.Scheduler, so no new attribute setup is required. Config plumbing is safe: RecomputeSchedulerConfig.initialize_from_config copies all SchedulerConfig fields dynamically, so max_num_active_seqs propagates. Schedulers that rely on super().schedule() (BatchJobAwareScheduler, ShortRequestFirstAsyncScheduler) inherit the new behavior with no change. Add a regression test that max_num_active_seqs is honored by each vendored schedule() path.
deep_analysis.risk: Low. The change is purely additive and default-preserving (None falls back to max_num_running_reqs), so existing Ascend deployments are unaffected. Main risk is silent feature gap: if the three vendored schedule() admission checks are not updated, users setting --max-num-active-seqs on Ascend get no admission cap while believing it is active; behavior differs from CUDA/ROCm. Minor risk of drift if future upstream schedule() refactors are copied again — the vendored loops should be updated alongside the upstream admission semantics. No crash, no interface/signature breakage.
